issues.legal_issue: A statutory occupancy grant to one member of a joint family does not, by itself, extinguish the other members’ rights to seek partition of the joint property in a civil court.
material_facts: The disputed lands formed part of properties held by a joint family, and the family members claimed shares by succession.
An occupancy right over some of the lands was granted in the name of one family member.
The family members brought a civil suit seeking partition, and the courts below upheld a jurisdictional objection based on the statutory scheme.
issues.conclusion: The statutory scheme does not oust the civil court’s jurisdiction to decide disputes about the respective rights of joint-family members claiming under the same title; the Act’s forum determines entitlement to occupancy rights, not those inter se rights.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 10, 24 and 29 of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Abolition of Inams Act, 1955 provide for determination of claims to occupancy rights and appeals from those determinations, but do not provide a forum for disputes between members of a joint family claiming under the same title. A statutory ouster of civil-court jurisdiction is strictly construed and extends only to matters the statutory forum is competent to decide. In light of Article 300A, property rights cannot be taken away except in accordance with law; Hindustan Petroleum Corpn. Ltd. v. Darius Shapur Chenai, (2005) 7 SCC 627, is relied on in this connection.

rule.if: partition_suit and joint_family_property and occupancy_right_granted_to_one_sharer and inter_se_family_share_dispute and statutory_forum_does_not_determine_inter_se_shares

predicates.partition_suit: A claimant brought a civil proceeding seeking division of property among alleged co-sharers.
predicates.joint_family_property: The disputed property was held as part of a joint family’s property.
predicates.occupancy_right_granted_to_one_sharer: An authority granted an occupancy right over the disputed property in the name of one family member.
predicates.inter_se_family_share_dispute: Family members claimed competing shares in the property under the same family title.
predicates.statutory_forum_does_not_determine_inter: The statutory forum was assigned the task of deciding entitlement to occupancy rights, not disputes between family members claiming under the same title.

issues.definition: When a partition suit concerns joint-family property, an occupancy right is recorded in one sharer’s name, the family members dispute their respective shares, and the statutory forum does not determine those shares, the civil court may adjudicate the partition rights.

issues.legal_issue: An occupancy right granted in the name of a member acting for a joint family can benefit the family as a whole and form part of the property available for partition.
material_facts: The disputed lands were among the joint family properties, and the family members inherited interests in those properties.
The occupancy right was granted in the name of one member, who was the only male member of the family and was treated as acting for the family in cultivating the lands.
The grant was made under a provision that treated the occupancy right as effective from the date the lands vested in the State.
issues.conclusion: Where the occupancy right is granted to a member as representing the joint family, it enures to the benefit of the family and is partible.
issues.legal_principle: The word “person” in the statutory scheme is not confined to an individual and can include a body or association of persons. Possession by one co-sharer is, in law, possession of all; Bhubaneshwar Prasad Narain Singh v. Sidheswar Mukherjee, (1971) 1 SCC 556, is relied on for that principle. The court also explains that the statutory grant’s deemed effective date must be given its full effect when assessing the family’s rights under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956.

rule.if: partition_suit and joint_family_property and occupancy_right_granted_to_family_representative and cultivation_or_possession_for_family

predicates.partition_suit: A claimant brought a civil proceeding seeking division of property among alleged co-sharers.
predicates.joint_family_property: The disputed property was held as part of a joint family’s property.
predicates.occupancy_right_granted_to_family_repres: An authority granted the occupancy right in the name of a member who represented the joint family.
predicates.cultivation_or_possession_for_family: The named member possessed or cultivated the land on behalf of the joint family.

issues.definition: When a partition suit concerns joint-family property and the named recipient obtained the occupancy right as the family’s representative while possessing or cultivating the land for the family, the right benefits the family and is available for partition.

issues.legal_issue: A precedent that treats the named recipient of an occupancy grant as its sole beneficiary, without accounting for joint-family co-sharer rights, requires reconsideration by a larger bench.
material_facts: The courts below relied on an earlier Supreme Court decision in upholding the jurisdictional objection to the partition suit.
The Court concluded that the earlier decision had not correctly read a prior decision concerning the rights of co-sharers and had not correctly been applied to the statutory scheme at issue.
The Court considered that the precedent’s correctness required consideration by a larger bench.
issues.conclusion: The earlier precedent was not correctly rendered, and the matter was directed to be placed before a larger bench for consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Bhubaneshwar Prasad Narain Singh v. Sidheswar Mukherjee, (1971) 1 SCC 556, recognizes the co-sharer principle that possession of one co-sharer is possession of all. The Court held that Lokraj v. Kishan Lal, (1995) 3 SCC 291, had not correctly read that decision and had not correctly been applied to the statutory provisions governing occupancy grants and inter se family disputes; it therefore required consideration by a larger bench.

predicates.partition_suit: A claimant brought a civil proceeding seeking division of property among alleged co-sharers.
predicates.lower_court_relied_on_precedent_to_bar_c: A lower court relied on an earlier judicial decision to hold that the civil court lacked jurisdiction.
predicates.precedent_treats_named_grantee_as_sole_b: The earlier decision was read as treating the person named in the occupancy grant as its sole beneficiary.
predicates.statutory_forum_does_not_determine_inter: The statutory forum was assigned the task of deciding entitlement to occupancy rights, not disputes between family members claiming under the same title.

issues.definition: When a lower court relies on a precedent treating the named grantee as the sole beneficiary to bar a partition suit, although the statutory forum does not decide family members’ respective shares, the precedent requires larger-bench reconsideration.
